The patch's only out-of-footprint hunk is `tests/test_ultra_run_task_test_cmds.py`, changing `{"cmd": "weird-runner tests/x", "runner": None, "ok": False}` to `"runner": "weird-runner"`. That edit is not optional and not scope creep: M5 requires `runner_for` to report the first whitespace-delimited word as the runner for any command outside the three built-in prefixes, which directly contradicts the `runner: None` the BASE test pinned. The global constraint "The existing compiler, preflight and launcher exams keep passing in every clone" carries a Check that runs exactly this file, so leaving it untouched would have made that (blocking) check red — the two constraints are only jointly satisfiable by editing the file. The change is minimal and disclosed with an in-place comment citing #644, and it preserves the leg's meaning (`ok is False`, `returncode == 1`), so the exam still fails if the red verdict is lost. The defect is the task's own text: `tests/test_ultra_run_task_test_cmds.py` belongs in Task 1's Files block. No edit inside this task's declared FILES answers it, hence actor `plan` and `minor` — the global constraint it brushes ("No file outside a task's own Files block is edited") carries no `Check:` the driver ran, and every Check that was run exited 0.

Everything the task requires is otherwise mapped to the diff: M1 to `exam_shape_violations` (message begins `exam-shape: task <id>`, names the unrunnable path, contains `Exam command`) wired into both `collect_violations` and `main`'s `grammar_violations` so `--check` exits 2, exercised by `test_peer_task_with_unrunnable_proof_path_and_no_exam_command_is_refused`; M2 to the peer-and-unmatched pairing (`review != peer` and built-in-shape cases, plus the peer-with-no-Test-path case, all asserting `PLAN OK`/exit 0); M3 to `derive_task_test_cmd(proof_tests, exam_command)` and the `exam_command` threaded into the wave entry's `testCmd`, exercised by the five-task declared/silent pair that pins one row per built-in shape and null for the Run-only task; M4 to `exam_command_violations`' `count(EXAM_PATHS_TOKEN) != 1`; M5 to `runner_for`'s new first-word/`command -v` fall-through, exercised end-to-end through `--validate-knobs` with a PATH holding an executable `zig` stub and a PATH that lacks it (green/red plus non-zero exit), and by the direct three-prefix tuple assertions; M6 to the new `## The document` paragraph, confirmed by the two `sed | grep -q` Run: commands. Both Produces symbols exist with the stated signatures and are called directly by `test_parse_exam_command_reads_the_header_line_and_only_the_header` and `test_exam_command_violations_pins_the_token_count`. The `_plan_claim_raw` refactor into `_plan_header_value(md_text, read_label)` is behaviour-preserving (the `value is not None` guard keeps an empty label value from being dropped the way a truthiness test would). No shouted imperative was added to the skill, `fleet/launch.mjs` is untouched, and no file present at BASE is deleted.; Out-of-FILES edit: the diff modifies `tests/test_ultra_run_task_test_cmds.py:153`, which is not in this task's Files block (`test_an_unrecognised_runner_fails_the_line` is re-pinned from `"runner": None` to `"runner": "weird-runner"`). The edit itself is correct and unavoidable — M5 mandates that a command matching no built-in prefix now reports its first word as the runner, which directly contradicts that BASE assertion, and the global constraint `Check:` command runs exactly that file, so it had to change for the check to pass. The defect is in the task text: the Files block should have listed `tests/test_ultra_run_task_test_cmds.py` as a Modify. The updated assertion still pins the observable red verdict (`ok: False`, exit 1), so nothing is weakened. One leftover: that file's docstring near line 280 still describes an unmatched command as `"runner": null, "ok": false`, now stale prose.; Duplicated shape classification in `skills/ultrapowers/scripts/compile_plan.py`: the new `_known_proof_shape(path)` re-lists MJS/PY/BUN_PROOF_TEST_RE, while `derive_task_test_cmd`'s own loop encodes the same "is this runnable" judgement in its if/elif/else fallthrough. The two must agree or the refusal drifts from the derivation — add a fourth shape to the derivation loop and forget the predicate, and `exam_shape_violations` refuses a peer plan whose exam the table can in fact run (or, the other way, a peer task silently loses its examiner with no refusal). Route the loop's fallthrough through the same predicate so there is one source of truth. Nothing in this diff is wrong today; this is about the next shape.; concern: out-of-FILES: tests/test_ultra_run_task_test_cmds.py — leg (b) (`test_an_unrecognised_runner_fails_the_line`) asserted the exact fall-through M5 replaces: `{"cmd": "weird-runner tests/x", "runner": None, "ok": False}`. plan-defect: the ladder the diff mirrors is wider than the preflight's at the `package.json` rung, so the refusal has a hole the Claim wants closed. `skills/ultrapowers/scripts/ultra_run.py:65-82` (`detect_test_cmd`) only *decides* on `package.json` when it carries a `scripts.test` entry, or when a `bun.lock`/`bun.lockb` sits beside it; a `package.json` with neither falls through to the Makefile/`go.mod`/`Cargo.toml` rungs. `fleet/launch.mjs`'s new `TOOLCHAIN_LADDER` rung `{ manifest: 'package.json', toolchain: null }` has no `holds`, so any `package.json` at all stops the ladder. Concretely: a Go repo with a JS frontend whose `package.json` declares no `test` script and has no bun lockfile is *not* refused on the laptop, and the VM's preflight then derives `go test ./...` and dies on the box — the exact failure #645's decision 1 ("Say it up front") asks the launcher to pre-empt, and a contradiction of this task's own Context sentence "the launcher mirrors that ladder's order exactly". This is the task's text rather than the implementer's choice: M5 says flatly "A checkout holding `package.json` beside `go.mod` is not refused on the toolchain" and Proof leg (e) fixes the fixture as "`package.json` (an empty object) beside `go.mod`", so the faithful mirror (`{}` has no `scripts.test`, therefore the `go.mod` rung decides, therefore refuse `toolchain go`) is precisely what the exam forbids. No edit inside `fleet/launch.mjs` can close the hole and keep leg (e) green, which is why the actor is `plan` and not `implementer`. Nothing regresses relative to BASE (which refused no target on toolchain at all), so this is advisory, not blocking. To settle it the plan would have to restate M5 and leg (e) — e.g. leg (e)'s first case becomes `package.json` holding `{"scripts": {"test": "vitest run"}}` beside `go.mod` (still not refused, still the earlier rung), plus a new case pinning `{}` beside `go.mod` as refused with `toolchain go` — and `fleet/launch.mjs`'s `package.json` rung would gain a `holds` reading `JSON.parse(text)?.scripts?.test` with a bun-lockfile fallback, matching `ultra_run.py:66-82`.

EXAM EDITED, resolved: the hunk the implementer applied to the peer-written exam is confined to leg (b), replacing the `engine=<sha> (pinned)` pin with a `deepEqual` against BASE's four lines plus a negative assertion that the tip annotation never appears; legs (a), (c) and (d) stand as the exam writer left them (verbatim main-tip line, recorded `git ls-remote <ENGINE_URL> HEAD` call, full-equality comment pins in both legs, the `new`-argv quote-shape check, the JSON round trip, the third `--overlap`/`--tier` launch, and the sentinel). '), baseLines(result))` at lines 330-333 and 365-368) and would need the same relaxation.; `renderLaunch` now filters the assembled array with `(line) => line !== null` (fleet/launch.mjs:462), which silently drops any field that is itself `null` — at BASE all four fields were joined unconditionally, so a null `vm` would have rendered as the string "null". [] : [engineLine(result)])`, or building the array with `.concat`) keeps the other four lines unfilterable.
